meta.title: Redis Command Reference - S-Jiffy
meta.description: 100+ common Redis commands with search and category filtering; click a card to copy the command syntax.
desc: 100+ common Redis commands with search and category filtering; click a card to copy the command syntax.
ui.2: Click any command card to copy its full syntax.
ui.5: Returns stream structural info (length, first/last IDs, consumer groups, etc.).
ui.6: Reassign messages pending beyond the timeout to specified consumers.
ui.7: Shows details of pending messages in a consumer group.
ui.8: Acknowledges processed messages, removing them from the Pending list.
ui.9: Manages consumer groups: create, set, destroy, add/remove consumers.
ui.10: Trims a stream: MAXLEN truncates by length, MINID deletes messages below a threshold.
ui.11: Deletes one or more messages from a stream.
ui.12: Reads new messages from one or more streams; $ reads only newly written ones.
ui.13: Returns messages by ID in descending order.
ui.14: Returns messages by ID range; - and + mean the smallest/largest ID.
ui.15: Returns the number of messages in a stream.
ui.16: Appends a stream message; * auto-generates the ID (millisecond timestamp-sequence).
ui.17: Stores GEOSEARCH results in a sorted set (can include distance).
ui.18: Queries members inside a circle or box, with sorting and count limits.
ui.19: Returns geohash strings (11-char standard) for member positions.
ui.20: Queries members within a radius around a member (deprecated, use GEOSEARCH).
ui.21: Queries members within a radius around given coordinates (deprecated, use GEOSEARCH).
ui.22: Computes the distance between two members, default in meters.
ui.23: Returns the longitude/latitude coordinates of members.
ui.24: Adds geographic members (longitude first, latitude second).
ui.25: Lists currently active channels, optionally filtered by pattern.
ui.26: Unsubscribes from specified patterns; no arguments unsubscribes from all.
ui.27: Unsubscribes from specified channels; no arguments unsubscribes from all.
ui.28: Subscribes to channels by pattern (supports * wildcards).
ui.29: Subscribes to one or more channels, entering listen mode.
ui.30: Publishes a message to a channel, returning the number of receivers.
ui.32: Watches keys; if any watched key is modified before the transaction executes, the transaction aborts (optimistic locking).
ui.33: Discards all queued commands in the transaction and exits it.
ui.34: Executes all queued commands in order, returning an array of each command's result.
ui.35: Starts a transaction; subsequent commands are queued rather than executed immediately.
ui.36: Lists client information for the current connection.
ui.37: Handshake protocol version (e.g. 3), also returns server info.
ui.38: Atomically swaps all data between two databases.
ui.39: Resets the current connection state (exits MULTI, cancels WATCH, deauthenticates, etc.).
ui.40: Asks the server to close the current connection.
ui.41: Switches databases (0-15, count determined by configuration).
ui.43: Probes connection liveness, optionally returning a custom message.
ui.44: Authenticates the connection; Redis 6+ supports username/password pair.
ui.45: Updates a key's last access time (works with the LRU eviction policy).
ui.46: Copies a key to a target key (can cross databases), without the TTL.
ui.47: Moves a key to another database (unavailable in cluster mode).
ui.48: Rebuilds a key from DUMP-serialized data; ttl 0 means never expires.
ui.49: Serializes a key value, returning a binary dump in RDB format.
ui.50: Returns the number of keys in the current database.
ui.52: Incrementally iterates keys in the database, returning a new cursor and a batch of keys each time.
ui.53: Returns all keys matching a pattern; use with caution in production (blocking), prefer SCAN.
ui.54: Renames a key only if the target does not exist, returning 1 on success.
ui.55: Renames a key, overwriting the target if it exists.
ui.56: Returns the type of value stored at a key (string/list/set/zset/hash/stream, etc.).
ui.57: Removes a key's TTL so it never expires.
ui.58: Returns the remaining time to live in milliseconds.
ui.59: Returns the remaining time to live in seconds; -1 means no TTL, -2 means the key does not exist.
ui.60: Sets the key to expire at a specified absolute time (milliseconds).
ui.62: Sets the key to expire at a specified absolute time (seconds).
ui.63: Sets a second-precision TTL, with NX/XX/GT/LT conditions.
ui.64: Counts how many of the given keys exist.
ui.65: Deletes keys asynchronously, freeing memory without blocking the main thread.
ui.66: Deletes one or more keys, returning the number deleted.
ui.67: Computes the intersection of multiple sorted sets and stores it in a target key.
ui.68: Computes the union of multiple sorted sets and stores it in a target key, with weights.
ui.69: Returns random members, optionally with their scores.
ui.70: Pops the highest-score member (or a specified count).
ui.71: Pops the lowest-score member (or a specified count).
ui.72: Returns the rank of a member by score in descending order (0-based).
ui.73: Returns the rank of a member by score in ascending order (0-based).
ui.74: Returns members in lexicographical order, requiring all members to have the same score.
ui.75: Returns members in a score range, ordered from high to low.
ui.76: Returns members in an index range, ordered from high to low.
ui.77: Returns members by index (or score/lex order), supporting reverse and with scores.
ui.78: Returns the count of members with scores in a range.
ui.79: Returns the number of members in a sorted set.
ui.80: Increments a member's score by a given amount.
ui.83: Adds or updates sorted set members and their scores.
ui.85: Computes the difference of sets and stores it in a target key.
ui.86: Returns the difference between the first set and the rest.
ui.87: Computes the union of sets and stores it in a target key.
ui.88: Returns the union of multiple sets.
ui.89: Returns the cardinality of the intersection, with an optional early-stop LIMIT.
ui.90: Computes the intersection of sets and stores it in a target key.
ui.91: Returns the intersection of multiple sets.
ui.92: Atomically moves a member from the source set to the destination set.
ui.93: Returns a random member (or a specified count) without removing; negative count may return duplicates.
ui.94: Removes and returns a random member (or a specified count).
ui.95: Returns the cardinality of a set.
ui.96: Checks whether a member is in the set, returning 1 if so.
ui.97: Returns all members of a set; note large sets block.
ui.98: Removes one or more members from a set.
ui.99: Adds one or more members to a set, returning how many were actually added.
ui.100: Incrementally iterates hash fields, suitable for large hashes.
ui.101: Returns one or more random fields (optionally with values).
ui.102: Returns the byte length of a field value.
ui.103: Increments a field value by a given float.
ui.104: Increments a field value by a given integer.
ui.105: Returns all values in a hash.
ui.106: Returns all field names in a hash.
ui.107: Returns the number of fields in a hash.
ui.108: Checks whether a field exists, returning 1 if so.
ui.109: Deletes one or more fields, returning the number deleted.
ui.110: Sets multiple fields in bulk (deprecated; HSET already supports multiple fields).
ui.111: Returns the values of multiple fields at once; missing fields return nil.
ui.112: Returns all fields and values in a hash; note large hashes block.
ui.113: Returns the value of a specified field in a hash.
ui.114: Sets a value only if the field does not exist, returning 1 on success.
ui.115: Sets one or more fields in a hash, returning the number of newly added fields.
ui.116: Returns the index of the first occurrence of an element in a list, with rank and count arguments.
ui.117: Blocking version of LMOVE, waiting up to the timeout for an element to pop.
ui.118: Blocking version of RPOPLPUSH (deprecated, use BLMOVE instead).
ui.119: Blockingly pops an element from the tail, listening on multiple lists.
ui.120: Blocking pop: pops an element from the head of a non-empty list, waiting until the timeout.
ui.121: Atomically pops an element from one list and pushes it to a specified end of another.
ui.122: Pops the tail element of source and pushes it to the head of destination (deprecated, use LMOVE instead).
ui.123: Deletes elements equal to the given value; positive/negative count sets the direction from head or tail.
ui.124: Inserts a new element before or after a pivot element.
ui.125: Keeps only elements within the specified index range and deletes the rest.
ui.126: Modifies the value of an element at a specified index.
ui.127: Returns the element at a specified index, supporting negative indexes.
ui.128: Returns elements in a specified index range.
ui.129: Returns the length of a list.
ui.130: Pops one (or a specified count of) element(s) from the tail.
ui.131: Pops one (or a specified count of) element(s) from the head.
ui.132: Pushes an element to the tail only if the list exists.
ui.133: Pushes one or more elements to the tail of a list.
ui.134: Pushes an element to the head only if the list exists.
ui.135: Pushes one or more elements to the head of a list.
ui.136: Performs multiple bit-field read/write/increment operations on a string.
ui.137: Finds the position of the first bit that is 0 or 1.
ui.138: Performs bitwise operations across multiple keys and stores the result in a target key.
ui.139: Counts the number of bits set to 1 in a string.
ui.140: Returns the bit value at a given offset in a string.
ui.141: Sets the bit at an offset (0 or 1), returning the original bit value.
ui.142: Computes the longest common subsequence of two strings, returning its length or index info.
ui.143: Returns the byte length of a string value.
ui.144: Decrements a key value by a given integer.
ui.145: Decrements a key value by 1; the value must be an integer.
ui.146: Increments a key value by a given float, returning the result as a string.
ui.147: Increments a key value by a given integer.
ui.148: Increments a key value by 1; the value must be an integer, a missing key counts as 0.
ui.149: Appends content to the end of a key value, returning the new string length.
ui.150: Sets a key value with a millisecond TTL, atomically.
ui.151: Sets a key value with a second TTL, atomically.
ui.152: Sets a value only if the key does not exist, returning 1 on success and 0 on failure.
ui.153: Sets multiple key-value pairs at once only if none of the keys exist.
ui.154: Sets multiple key-value pairs at once, atomically.
ui.155: Returns the values of multiple keys at once; missing keys return nil.
ui.156: Sets a new value and returns the old one (deprecated, use SET ... GET instead).
ui.157: Overwrites part of a string starting at an offset.
ui.158: Returns a substring, 0-based, supporting negative indexes.
ui.159: Returns the key value and updates its TTL; PERSIST clears the TTL.
ui.160: Returns the key value and deletes the key at the same time.
ui.161: Returns the string value of a key; a missing key returns nil.
ui.162: Sets a key value; NX writes only if the key is absent, XX only if present, with optional TTL.
